claim: Native syllable structure is (C)V(ː): a syllable contains one short or long vowel, optionally preceded by one consonant.
formal_environment: (C)V(ː)
normalized_environment: (C)V(ː)
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Borrowings can contain codas and are treated separately.
publication_page: Direct LaTeX source; printed page not recovered

claim: A native syllable cannot contain two or more vowels; all non-identical VV sequences are analyzed as separate syllables rather than diphthongs.
formal_environment: *VV within σ; V.V across syllables
normalized_environment: *VV within σ; V.V across syllables
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Older descriptions sometimes analyze ai/au/oi as diphthongs; the grammar rejects that analysis using reduplication, stress and metrical evidence.
publication_page: Direct LaTeX source; printed page not recovered

claim: Reduplication supports disyllabic analysis of VV: /kai/ can form /kakai/ by copying the first syllable /ka-/.
formal_environment: ka.i -> ka~ka.i
normalized_environment: ka.i -> ka~ka.i
publication_page: Direct LaTeX source; printed page not recovered

claim: Stress also diagnoses VV as disyllabic: when the final syllable is short, the penultimate vowel receives stress even inside sequences that could phonetically resemble diphthongs.
formal_environment: final L -> penultimate σ stress, including V.V
normalized_environment: final L -> penultimate σ stress, including V.V

claim: Short vowels are monomoraic/light and long vowels are bimoraic/heavy; onset consonants do not contribute moraic weight.
formal_environment: V=1μ; Vː=2μ; onset C=0μ
normalized_environment: V=1μ; Vː=2μ; onset C=0μ
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Loan coda consonants are also described as non-moraic.

claim: All morae are parsed into trochaic feet, and a foot cannot span a syllable boundary.

claim: All non-initial feet must be bimoraic; only the initial foot may be degenerate/monomoraic.

claim: The grammar treats the metrical constraints as inviolable across native words, reduplications, compounds and borrowings: a heavy syllable is never followed by an odd number of morae.
